appraisal_events.evidence: « mon absence de disposition pour les lettres, pressentie jadis du côté de Guermantes, confirmée durant ce séjour dont c'était le dernier soir [...] me parut quelque chose de moins regrettable » ; « l'état maladif qui allait me confiner dans une maison de santé » ; et, devant Gilberte, « j'ai trop mauvais caractère [...] j'ai été fiancé, mais je n'ai pas pu ».
appraisal_events.explanation: On the eve of departure the narrator judges himself and confirms his lack of literary vocation, his coming confinement in a sanatorium, and his incapacity for marriage; the diminishment is self-administered and the narration endorses rather than distances it.

appraisal_events.evidence: « l'auteur de ce livre sur Whistler où vraiment le faire, le coloriage artiste de l'original Américain est souvent rendu avec une grande délicatesse par l'amoureux de tous les raffinements, de toutes les joliesses de la chose peinte qu'est Verdurin » ; l'hôtel du quai Conti « que son possesseur prétend être l'ancien hôtel des Ambassadeurs de Venise » ; la margelle « que Verdurin soutient être absolument du plus beau Sansovino ».
appraisal_events.explanation: The transcribed Goncourt pages raise Verdurin into a serious critic, connoisseur and princely host of a quasi-Venetian palace, a standing far above the figure the narrator's own account gives him. The verbs « prétend » and « soutient », the confessed renunciation of writing, and the guests who thought him « tout à fait inférieur » to Sainte-Beuve and Charles Blanc keep the elevation visibly ironized.

status_effects.explanation: His own verdict on himself lowers him locally: no gift for letters, bad character, an engagement he could not carry through.

The whole framing evening is governed by sadness — the unvisited church of Combray, thoughts of his own death, the prospect of the maison de santé — and the reading brings no relief, only a mixed impression.

Within the quoted diary Verdurin is treated as an authoritative art critic and grand host, which raises him locally; the ironic frame and the reported judgment of his inferiority keep the rise short of a full elevation.

ambiguities: The Goncourt pages are transcribed without in-text commentary, and the narrator prefaces them only as « une impression assez vive et mêlée » ; whether the frame endorses or undercuts their admiring portrait of Verdurin is genuinely left open, which is why the elevation is scored as ironized and modest rather than as a clear +2.

The narrator's self-diminishment is entangled with a devaluation of literature itself (« comme si la littérature ne révélait pas de vérité profonde »), so the passage can be read either as lowering him or as lowering the standard by which he judges himself; the immediately following « j'avais envie de les voir » reopens the question without resolving it.
